chapter_title: Nelson Mandela: Long Walk to Freedom

details: Held at the sandstone amphitheatre in Pretoria's Union Buildings.
Dignitaries and world leaders from over 140 countries attend to mark the birth of South Africa's first non-racial democratic government.
Swearing-in sequence: Mr. Klerk (Second Deputy President), Thabo Mbeki (First Deputy President), and Nelson Mandela (President).
evidence_or_examples: Mandela's pledge to obey and uphold the constitution and devote himself to the well-being of the republic.

details: South African jets, helicopters, and troop carriers fly in perfect formation over the Union Buildings.
Highest military generals, wearing medals, salute Mandela, signifying the military's submission to democratic rule.
Impala jets leave a colorful smoke chevron of the new South African flag (black, red, green, gold, blue, white).
evidence_or_examples: Generals who would have arrested Mandela in earlier years now saluting him as head of state.

branches.theme: Mandela's Political Philosophy and Human Rights

sub_branches.concept: Definition of True Courage and Tribute to Martyrs
details: Courage is not the absence of fear, but triumph over it.
Mandela pays homage to anti-apartheid freedom fighters like Oliver Tambo, Walter Sisulu, Chief Luthuli, Yusuf Dadoo, Bram Fischer, and Robert Sobukwe.
He asserts that the extra-ordinary brutality of apartheid produced men of extraordinary courage and character.
evidence_or_examples: Mandela: 'The brave man is not he who does not feel afraid, but he who conquers that fear.'

sub_branches.concept: Twin Obligations and Evolution of Freedom
details: Every man has twin obligations: 1) To family, parents, wife, children; 2) To community, people, and country.
Under apartheid, Black South Africans attempting to fulfill social duties were forcibly separated from their families.
Mandela's understanding of freedom evolved from boyhood physical freedom (swimming, running) to youth personal freedom (earning a living) to adult collective freedom (liberating all Black citizens).
evidence_or_examples: Joining the African National Congress (ANC) when he saw his people's freedom curtailed.

details: An oppressor who deprives another of freedom is trapped behind bars of hatred, prejudice, and narrow-mindedness.
Both oppressor and oppressed are stripped of their core humanity and require liberation.
evidence_or_examples: Mandela's statement: 'The oppressed and the oppressor alike are robbed of their humanity.'

branches.theme: Poetic Study: A Tiger in the Zoo by Leslie Norris

sub_branches.concept: Dual Imagery of Captivity vs Natural Freedom
details: In the zoo: The tiger stalks the few steps of his concrete cell in quiet rage, locked behind steel bars, ignoring visitors.
In the wild: He should be lurking in shadows, sliding through long grass near water holes to ambush fat deer, or snarling around houses at the jungle edge to terrify villagers.
evidence_or_examples: Lines contrasting 'locked in a concrete cell' with 'lurking in shadow, sliding through long grass'.
